implementation_summary: Authored src/engine/receive-engine.ts (the per-group receive-engine FSM: createReceiveEngine(deps) -> {start, stop, reset, subscribe, getState}) implementing fsm.md's full transition table -- 8 lifecycle states as a {lifecycle, health} pair (health computed from an internal degradation-reason Set, never encoded as a lifecycle value, I-FSM-1), L1-L11 lifecycle transitions, H1/H2 health transitions, the gap-free catching_up->buffering_live->live cutover protocol (openLive() called before catchUp() on every entry per I-FSM-2/AC-FSM-2; live signals buffered during catching_up/buffering_live and applied in arrival order once draining, I-FSM-3), the T_join=8000ms joining-gate with background-continue-and-late-merge (bootstrap fetch modeled as one adapter.catchUp() call raced against an injected EngineScheduler's setTimeout, never cancelled on timeout), and the L8/L9 epoch-triggered deferred-retry flow (I-FSM-6: fires only on group_epoch_advanced with a non-empty deferred queue, never on group_ratchet_advanced -- which the 'skipped' IngestSignal now emits). All signal processing (historical drain, buffered-live drain, direct-live application, deferred-retry) is funneled through a single internal FIFO promise chain (`enqueue`) to guarantee ordering under concurrent arrival. The engine is projection-free by design (holds no in-memory TaskProjection; emits domain_event_accepted for the integration layer to fold via applyEvent) and imports only src/domain/domain-events.ts's derive*AcceptedEventId helpers plus src/domain/task-events.ts's TaskEvent type, consuming IngestSource/PersistenceAdapter purely through their interfaces. Authored src/engine/ingest-policy.ts (createIngestPolicy): a dedupe gate (hasProcessed/markProcessed on derived AcceptedDomainEvent ids, closing AC-FSM-8's exactly-once-emission property) plus a deferred/retry-budget queue (enqueueDeferred/retryBatch/recordAttempt/isExhausted/pruneDeferred) that ports PendingRetryQueue's cap+evict-eldest+TTL-prune algorithm to engine-native RawProtocolFact/factId types rather than importing src/marmot/ingest-queue.ts directly, which engine-boundary.structural.test.ts's AC-BOUND-1 scanner unconditionally forbids for any file under src/engine/ (verified against the scanner source; documented as a judgment call). Both files typecheck clean and pass the pre-existing engine-boundary.structural.test.ts (AC-BOUND-1/AC-BOUND-3) as-is.

judgment_calls: ingest-policy.ts ports (does not import) PendingRetryQueue's algorithm from src/marmot/ingest-queue.ts, because AC-BOUND-1's structural scanner unconditionally forbids any src/engine/* file from importing anything matching '/marmot/'. See architecture.json 'ingest-policy-cannot-import-marmot-ingest-queue'.

The engine stays projection-free by explicit design choice (Constraint 7 permits this); tests fold emitted domain_event_accepted events with the real task-projector.applyEvent to stand in for the integration layer where an AC talks about 'the projection'. See architecture.json 'engine-stays-projection-free'.

IngestSource exposes no dedicated bootstrap-fetch method, so the joining-phase bootstrap fetch is modeled as one adapter.catchUp() call raced against T_join, distinct from the separate openLive()+catchUp() cycle every catching_up entry performs for the cutover drain. See architecture.json 'bootstrap-fetch-is-a-catchup-call-raced-against-t-join' and verification.json VQ-S5-017 (post-impl).

recovering's (L1) entry action performs a functionally coherent but not AC-REC-exhaustive R1-R3 pass (rebuilds the deferred queue per R2a/R2, resubmits only the seq>watermark crash-gap tail per R3) -- AC-REC-1..9 belong to S11. See architecture.json 'recovering-r1-r3-best-effort-not-full-ac-rec-coverage'.

Both test files mock all ten PersistenceAdapter methods in-memory (replicating raw-event-log-store.ts's exact algorithm) rather than importing the real S4 store, since that import is ALSO forbidden under src/engine/ by the same AC-BOUND-1 scanner. See verification.json VQ-S5-018 (post-impl).

retrospective.harder_than_needed: Two aspects of the story brief were in direct tension with hard, pre-existing structural gates that this story's new files were told they 'must pass as-is': (1) the instruction to wrap PendingRetryQueue from src/marmot/ingest-queue.ts is unconditionally forbidden by engine-boundary.structural.test.ts's AC-BOUND-1 scanner for ANY file under src/engine/, verified directly against the scanner's source and its own liveness fixture proving that exact import shape flips it to failing; (2) the instruction that 'fact/accepted-event persistence uses the real S4 raw-event-log-store... in integration-style tests' is equally impossible for any TEST file under src/engine/, since the scanner has no test-file carve-out and also forbids '/persistence/' imports. Both required reading the scanner's actual source code (not just the AC prose) to confirm the constraint was absolute before committing to a workaround, and both were resolved the same way -- porting the proven algorithm/behavior rather than importing across the forbidden boundary -- mirroring engine-types.ts's own S1 precedent for exactly this situation (declaring a structural NostrEvent type instead of importing applesauce-core's). A second, more subtle issue was a genuine implementation bug caught only by TDD: routing the L8/L9 deferred-retry pass's per-signal handling through the same `enqueue()` serial-chain helper used everywhere else created a real deadlock, because runDeferredRetryPass only ever executes from within a job that is ITSELF already running as an enqueued job (reached via handleEpochAdvanced <- processSignal <- enqueue) -- the nested enqueue call chained a new job behind the very job awaiting it. This was caught by receive-engine.fsm.test.ts's AC-INV-5 test hanging (not a clean assertion failure), diagnosed by tracing the promise chain, and fixed by calling the handler directly rather than re-entering enqueue() from an already-serialized context.
retrospective.surprised_by: The AC-FSM-8 property test's initial numRuns=100 run was not hanging but was simply slow enough (~5.26s) to trip the vitest default 5000ms per-test timeout, entirely due to vi.waitFor's polling interval overhead multiplied across 100 runs -- replacing it with an event-driven wait (resolving a Promise from inside the engine's own subscribe callback, zero poll interval) dropped the same 100-run property test to 13ms. Separately, the SAME polling-vs-event-driven distinction surfaced a genuine test-authoring race: waiting only for the 'catching_up' lifecycle event (which fires synchronously inside transitionTo, before its own internal `await persistence.saveCheckpoint(...)`) is NOT sufficient proof that adapter.openLive() has actually been called yet (that happens on the next line of enterCatchingUp, after transitionTo's await resolves) -- a live signal pushed in that narrow window is silently dropped by a test's mock adapter (onSignal still null), which is exactly what caused an early property-test counterexample (a live fact simply vanishing). Fixed by exposing an explicit 'live subscription is actually open' signal from the mock and awaiting that instead.

decider_caveats: FAST PATH retry-then-pass: 19/19 YES after two doc-only PARTIALs remediated (architecture.json judgment-call supersession note; keep-in-sync mock comment).
